provenance.l: Phoenix EDL reconstruction (NASA) — entry 5,516 m/s at −13.16°, 572.7 kg, β 65 kg/m² (Cd·A = m/β); chute 227.7 s at 10.79 km areodetic (13.4 km above the −2.64 km site), lander separation 404.85 s, touchdown 446 s at 2.5 m/s

Phoenix EDL as researched for pass 2 (docs/wip/2026-11-23-mars-landings-record.md): 11.8 m disk-gap-band at about 12.6 km (13.4 km above the site in the reconstruction above); heat shield 15–25 s later (20 s drawn) with the legs out; separation from the backshell at about 980 m (960 m in the reconstruction); 12 pulsed thrusters to 2.4 m/s. The leg-deploy delay, the radar lock (2.4 km, InSight's figure) and the time the arrays opened are drawn, not sourced
